brief.prompt: Retrieve exterior and cockpit images for the P-51 and OH-6, and make both aircraft substantially more realistic and accurate.
brief.style: reference-informed realistic proportions and mechanical details, restrained procedural materials
brief.geometryBudget: under 60000 imported triangles; mechanical pivots retained
brief.collision: existing coarse aircraft probes; importer hull extraction capped at 128

method.geometry: deterministic three.js analytic sections, surface patches, mechanical parts and geometry lettering
method.textures: No bitmap textures or image-generation prompts; photographs used only as inspected references. All material response and printed scales are authored procedurally.

commands: node packages/tooling/dist/cli.mjs asset inspect molen.entities.aircraft.p51d --verify --project content/entities/project.json

visualReview: Inspected the imported GLB in eight turntable views, a lit apron, side detail and two seated panel views. Reviewed canopy visibility, padded coaming and reflector sight, asymmetric flight/engine instruments, side consoles and controls, bucket seat/harnesses, wing filler caps/access panels, cowling seams/fasteners and the retained P-51D silhouette.
limitations: Assisted game flight, bounded pitch/bank; not certified performance or exact cockpit replicas.
No autorotation, vortex-ring model, fuel/engine systems, aerobatics, weapons or crash deformation.
Physics uses coarse airframe probes against nearby resident geometry; imported hull extraction is capped at 128.
Cockpit controls are operated by the documented input bindings; most physical switches are visual details.
Reference-informed approximation combining restored aircraft and period references; not a serial-specific cockpit replica.
Most added engine/system instruments and switches are visual details; the pre-existing simulation bindings remain live.
The solver retains its level ground pose instead of a parked taildragger nose-up attitude.
